name: isoline-scene
summary: Split hero with Isoline's animated isometric scene beside the copy: a mechanical keyboard drawn in SVG hairlines that types by itself while keys dip under the pointer, on a grid floor that fades into the page. Thirteen other scenes (a city with traffic, a cargo port, a drone delivery, an exploded phone, your word as a dollhouse) are one option away. Plain SVG, no WebGL, no dependency; upstream pauses it off screen and holds a readable pose under reduced motion. With no script the frame rests on a faint isometric grid under an orange glow.

scene.description: city, supply, flight, delivery, port, line, product, steamer, cabinet, lockers, keyboard, interface, relief or word. examples/basic.html's choice.

azimuth.description: Camera turn in degrees. Upstream range; default from examples/basic.html.

elevation.description: Camera tilt in degrees. Upstream range; default from examples/basic.html.

accent.description: What moves or answers the pointer. examples/basic.html's colour.

plate.description: Ground colour, the stage background. Upstream default.

floor.description: Floor under the scene: none, grid or dots. examples/basic.html's choice.

floorStrength.description: 0 faint to 1 strong. Default from examples/basic.html.

density.description: 0 to 1, read by each scene its own way: traffic, typing speed, yard stacks. Upstream default.

stroke.description: Line width in px. Upstream default.

spin.description: Turntable: the camera circles the scene. Upstream default.

parallax.description: The camera leans a little towards the pointer. Upstream default.

interactive.description: The scene answers the pointer. Upstream default.

deviations.what: The README points script-tag users at the committed isoline.min.js, so that build is ported verbatim inside a named function isolineLib(t), which mount() calls once with window. Removed: the `!function(t){` IIFE head, the call that passed it window, and the `module.exports=or` and `t.Isoline=or` assignments at the end; the body returns the constructor `or` instead.
deviations.why: Seam. A paw-fx module touches no global at import time, and the bundle published itself onto window the moment it loaded.

deviations.what: mount(el, opts) appends a stage div to the section's frame and calls new Isoline(stage, opts) with examples/basic.html's settings (keyboard scene, azimuth 30, elevation 36, accent #ff6a3d, grid floor at strength 0.5) as defaults. update(next) is upstream's set(next). destroy() is upstream's destroy() plus removing the stage and data-fx-live. Reduced motion, the off-screen pause and every pointer response are upstream's.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream writes role, aria-label, its --il-* palette and a background onto the element it is given; a stage this module owns keeps all of that off the section.

deviations.what: The section is a split hero, copy beside a 16:10 frame that stacks under 760px. The resting frame is a faint isometric grid (lines at the two iso angles in upstream's mid tone #3e3e44 on its plate #08090a) under a soft glow in the accent, faded at its edges; upstream's own toSVG() frame was not baked in because, added to the 47 KB gzipped bundle, it crossed the 60 KB own-code cap.
deviations.why: Ours. A dark empty frame reads as broken before the script runs, and the copy is kept off the line work so it never sits on hairlines.
